records.shared_stimulus: A motion model shows equal-time dots moving farther apart to the right, with rightward velocity arrows growing longer.
parts: (a) Identify what the dot spacing indicates about speed.
(b) Identify what the arrow direction and length represent.
(c) Use (a) and (b) to decide whether velocity is changing.
(d) Write a short motion description consistent with all parts of the model.
records.student_text:
A motion model shows equal-time dots moving farther apart to the right, with rightward velocity arrows growing longer.
(a) Identify what the dot spacing indicates about speed.
(b) Identify what the arrow direction and length represent.
(c) Use (a) and (b) to decide whether velocity is changing.
(d) Write a short motion description consistent with all parts of the model.
records.student_html:
A motion model shows equal-time dots moving farther apart to the right, with rightward velocity arrows growing longer.

  1. Identify what the dot spacing indicates about speed.
  2. Identify what the arrow direction and length represent.
  3. Use (a) and (b) to decide whether velocity is changing.
  4. Write a short motion description consistent with all parts of the model.
Show your reasoning here.
records.answer: Speed increases; arrows show velocity direction and magnitude; velocity changes; object moves right while speeding up.
records.solution_text: Speed increases; arrows show velocity direction and magnitude; velocity changes; object moves right while speeding up.
records.solution_html: Speed increases; arrows show velocity direction and magnitude; velocity changes; object moves right while speeding up.

records.primary_i_can: I can compare velocity vectors to determine whether an object’s velocity is changing.
records.evidence_job: Interpret, construct, compare, or critique a motion representation while preserving the physical quantities and relationships in the target.
records.student_action: Use the supplied data/representation or construct the requested representation, then explain the motion evidence it shows.
records.intended_reasoning: Interpret, construct, compare, or critique a motion representation while preserving the physical quantities and relationships in the target.
records.student_text: Vector A is 4 cm long and points east. Vector B is 4 cm long and points north. Determine whether the object’s velocity changed and explain what feature of the vectors supports your answer.
records.student_html:
Vector A is 4 cm long and points east. Vector B is 4 cm long and points north. Determine whether the object’s velocity changed and explain what feature of the vectors supports your answer.

Show your reasoning here.
records.answer: Yes. The speed magnitude can be the same, but the direction changes from east to north, so velocity changes.
records.solution_text: Velocity vectors are equal only when both magnitude and direction are equal. Changing direction changes velocity.
records.solution_html: Velocity vectors are equal only when both magnitude and direction are equal. Changing direction changes velocity.

records.primary_i_can: I can connect motion diagrams, data tables, and graphs to written descriptions of motion and critique an incorrect motion model and revise it using evidence.
records.evidence_job: Interpret, construct, compare, or critique a motion representation while preserving the physical quantities and relationships in the target.

records.intended_reasoning: Interpret, construct, compare, or critique a motion representation while preserving the physical quantities and relationships in the target.
records.student_text: A position–time graph is shown. Write a motion description consistent with the graph, then identify one common incorrect interpretation and correct it.
records.student_html: A position–time graph is shown. Write a motion description consistent with the graph, then identify one common incorrect interpretation and correct it.
records.answer: The object moves in the positive direction at constant velocity 4 m/s. The graph height represents position, not physical height above the ground.
records.solution_text: The straight-line position–time graph has constant slope 4 m/s, so velocity is constant. The vertical axis is position, so it should not be read as a picture of a hill.
records.solution_html: The straight-line position–time graph has constant slope 4 m/s, so velocity is constant. The vertical axis is position, so it should not be read as a picture of a hill.
